prompt_v1:
Create a polished art-direction preview sheet for an original mobile strategy game called “4목” (gravity four-in-a-row). This is a concept for user feedback, not a finished screenshot. Wide landscape presentation, two coordinated panels on a plain warm off-white background: the LEFT 48% shows a large, beautifully designed original opponent character and desk; the RIGHT 52% shows ONE complete tall 9:16 mobile in-game UI concept, straight-on, without a device bezel. The actual mobile layout represents a 1080×1920 design canvas. Give both panels generous margins. Small discreet captions “CHARACTER” and “GAME UI” only if useful. Do not add paragraphs, diagrams, multiple variants or marketing copy.

ART DIRECTION: coherent hand-authored 2D pixel art, visible clean square pixel clusters, crisp nearest-neighbor edges, carefully controlled detail, no blurry interpolation, no vector-looking round blobs, no glossy 3D, no photorealism. Approachable barracks board-game competition, restrained palette of dark charcoal, deep army olive, muted sage, khaki, warm paper white, with tiny muted gold highlights. Excellent visual hierarchy, uncluttered and easy to use. Everything belongs to one consistent pixel-art world: character, desk, panels, buttons, cap and board. Simple restrained stepped corners on military panels, not busy tactical HUDs. No weapons, combat, blood, harsh warning red, distressed textures, national flags, real unit patches, official emblems, brand logos or real people. Camouflage is a newly invented pattern of simple olive/sage pixel clusters, not an exact real service uniform pattern.

CHARACTER, BOTH PANELS: the same adult male fictional Korean soldier, strong and confident rival, athletic broad shoulders, defined jaw, thick expressive eyebrows, composed slightly challenging expression, approachable enough for a casual puzzle game. Natural adult proportions, not chibi or a round emoji. He wears a well-constructed fitted military patrol cap with a flatish crown, short structured brim, side seams and an original small plain rectangular badge; a short-sleeve digital-camouflage T-shirt, not a long sleeve jacket. His ENTIRE UPPER BODY is visible from cap through head, neck, shoulders, chest, arms and waist at the desk edge. He is seated behind a simple olive wooden desk, with BOTH ELBOWS visibly supported on the tabletop, forearms naturally reaching forward and both hands relaxed on the desk. Anatomically clear elbows, hands and arm placement; not cropped at shoulders, not a floating head, not crossed arms hiding the elbows. No copyrighted character resemblance. On the left, show this large character/desk study with clean silhouette and lovingly designed pixel-art face, folds and cap. Keep enough resolution to assess the cap and camouflage.

MOBILE GAME UI (right): portrait 9:16, one complete usable in-game screen. A quiet warm-paper background with a restrained olive outer frame. Reserve a clear top host-navigation band, with a subtle gray host close capsule at its upper right; all game controls are BELOW this band and do not overlap it. Large centered Korean title “4목”, a small simple pause icon to its right. Below the title: a compact coherent opponent area featuring the SAME soldier's whole upper body, seated behind the thin desk, around one fifth of the game canvas height. A small centered rank label “훈련병” and a single gold star near the character, with no extra stats. A compact warm-paper speech strip underneath, short text “프로라고? 한 판 하자.” Keep it readable, do not fill screen with text.

The board is the dominant interaction area below the opponent: a square ivory/white board with uniform thin charcoal grid lines, black player disks and warm-white opponent disks outlined in charcoal. It is a gravity four-in-a-row board with SEVEN COLUMNS and SIX playable rows. Square spacing and square cells; use equal top/bottom margin inside the square outer board to accommodate the six rows. Show a simple unfinished game with only a few disks resting from the BOTTOM upward, no unsupported floating disks, not a red/yellow plastic Connect 4 product. Do not draw a 15×15 Gomoku board. A subtle translucent landing preview may appear in one selected column. Preserve broad clear touch targets.

Bottom controls are one aligned row of exactly three controls: a simple rectangular olive-outline button “되돌리기”, a larger ROUND dark-olive central button “놓기”, and a simple matching rectangle “다시하기”. Keep these straightforward with simple icons, comfortable spacing and consistent borders, no giant panel, no player avatar, no unrelated stats/currency/store/banner ad. Large legible essential labels only. Safe bottom margin. Character detail must not crowd the board. The overall result should feel like a premium small pixel-art military board game with calm readable mobile UI.
